I patched citation parsing and added a regression test for hierarchical review IDs plus bracket short hashes. Next I’m running focused tests, then I’ll re-record/confirm observe and continue the triage stages.

> TOOL

tool_use apply_patch
```json
{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Update File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/epic_triage_parsing.py\n@@\n-ISSUE_ID_RE = re.compile(r\"[a-z_]+::[a-f0-9]{8,}\")\n+ISSUE_ID_RE = re.compile(r\"[a-z_]+::[a-f0-9]{8,}\")\n+BRACKET_SHORT_ID_RE = re.compile(r\"\\[([a-z0-9_]{6,16})\\]\")\n@@\n def extract_issue_citations(text: str, valid_ids: set[str]) -> set[str]:\n     \"\"\"Extract issue IDs cited in free text.\n \n     Matches full issue IDs (e.g. ``review::abcdef12``) or bare 8+ char\n     hex suffixes that correspond to a known issue.\n     \"\"\"\n+    if not text or not valid_ids:\n+        return set()\n+\n     cited: set[str] = set()\n+\n+    # Prefer exact literal references for modern hierarchical IDs.\n+    for valid_id in valid_ids:\n+        if valid_id in text:\n+            cited.add(valid_id)\n+\n+    # Support bracketed short hashes used in queue displays, e.g. [planmode].\n+    short_map: dict[str, str] = {}\n+    ambiguous_short: set[str] = set()\n+    for valid_id in valid_ids:\n+        suffix = valid_id.rsplit(\"::\", 1)[-1]\n+        short = suffix[:8].lower()\n+        if not short:\n+            continue\n+        existing = short_map.get(short)\n+        if existing is None:\n+            short_map[short] = valid_id\n+        elif existing != valid_id:\n+            ambiguous_short.add(short)\n+\n+    for short in ambiguous_short:\n+        short_map.pop(short, None)\n+\n+    for short in BRACKET_SHORT_ID_RE.findall(text.lower()):\n+        mapped = short_map.get(short)\n+        if mapped:\n+            cited.add(mapped)\n+\n     # Match full issue IDs\n     for match in ISSUE_ID_RE.finditer(text):\n         candidate = match.group()\n         if candidate in valid_ids:\n             cited.add(candidate)\n*** End Patch\n"
}

noqa: F403\n+from desloppify.engine.plan_triage import (\n+    TRIAGE_CMD_RUN_STAGES_CLAUDE,\n+    TRIAGE_CMD_RUN_STAGES_CODEX,\n+    TRIAGE_IDS,\n+)\n+\n+\n+def triage_phase_banner(plan: PlanModel, state: dict | None = None) -> str:\n+    \"\"\"Return a banner string describing triage status.\"\"\"\n+    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)\n+    order = set(plan.get(\"queue_order\", []))\n+    has_triage = any(sid in order for sid in TRIAGE_IDS)\n+    meta = plan.get(\"epic_triage_meta\", {})\n+    run_hint = (\n+        f\"Run: {TRIAGE_CMD_RUN_STAGES_CODEX} \"\n+        f\"(or {TRIAGE_CMD_RUN_STAGES_CLAUDE})\"\n+    )\n+\n+    if not has_triage:\n+        if meta.get(\"triage_recommended\"):\n+            return (\n+                \"TRIAGE RECOMMENDED — review issues changed since last triage. \"\n+                f\"{run_hint}\"\n+            )\n+        return \"\"\n+\n+    if state and has_objective_backlog(state, None):\n+        return (\n+            \"TRIAGE PENDING — queued and will activate after objective work \"\n+            \"is complete.\"\n+        )\n+    stages = meta.get(\"triage_stages\", {})\n+    completed = [s for s in (\"observe\", \"reflect\", \"organize\", \"enrich\", \"sense-check\") if s in stages]\n+    if completed:\n+        return (\n+            f\"TRIAGE MODE ({len(completed)}/5 stages complete) — \"\n+            f\"complete all stages to exit. {run_hint}\"\n+        )\n+    return (\n+        \"TRIAGE MODE — review issues need analysis before fixing. \"\n+        f\"{run_hint}\"\n+    )\n+\n+\n+__all__ = PLAN_PUBLIC_EXPORTS\n*** End Patch\n"

> AGENT

I’ve mapped the starvation gap: deferrals are tracked only as a one-shot flag (`triage_recommended`) and endgame items are always hidden when objective work exists, so there’s no bounded escalation.  

Plan I’m implementing now:
1. Add shared defer-tracking helpers (`first_deferred_scan`, `defer_count`, deferred IDs, age checks) with scan/day escalation thresholds.
2. Update `sync_triage_needed` to persist triage defer metadata and, after threshold, escalate by injecting triage stages in priority order plus a force-visibility marker.
3. Update `sync_subjective_clusters` to persist subjective defer metadata and, after threshold, keep/promote deferred stale/under-target subjective IDs instead of evicting them.
4. Wire force-visibility through queue stamping/builders so lifecycle filtering can surface escalated triage/subjective items even when objective backlog exists.
5. Add/adjust direct tests for defer metadata, escalation behavior, and lifecycle forced-visibility rules; then run focused test slices and resolve the queue item.

not in stale_ids and item_id not in unscored_ids:\n            under_target.add(item_id)\n    return under_target\n\n\ndef review_issue_snapshot_hash(state: StateModel) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Hash open review/concerns issue IDs to detect triage-relevant changes.\"\"\"\n    review_ids = sorted(open_review_ids(state))\n    if not review_ids:\n        return \"\"\n    return hashlib.sha256(\"|\".join(review_ids).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]\n\n\ndef compute_new_issue_ids(plan: dict, state: StateModel) -> set[str]:\n    \"\"\"Return open review/concerns IDs that appeared since the last triage.\"\"\"\n    meta = plan.get(\"epic_triage_meta\", {})\n    triaged = set(meta.get(\"triaged_ids\", []))\n    return open_review_ids(state) - triaged if triaged else set()\n\n\ndef is_triage_stale(\n    plan: dict,\n    state: StateModel,\n) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Return True when genuinely new review issues appeared since last triage.\n\n    In-progress triage (confirmed stages + stage IDs in queue) is NOT\n    considered stale — the lifecycle filter in the work queue already\n    forces triage stages to the front.\n    \"\"\"\n    meta = plan.get(\"epic_triage_meta\", {})\n    triaged_ids = set(meta.get(\"triaged_ids\", []))\n    return bool(open_review_ids(state) - triaged_ids)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"compute_new_issue_ids\",\n    \"current_stale_ids\",\n    \"current_under_target_ids\",\n    \"current_unscored_ids\",\n    \"is_triage_stale\",\n    \"open_review_ids\",\n    \"review_issue_snapshot_hash\",\n]\nPYCODE"

  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/languages/_framework/treesitter/analysis/complexity_callbacks.py\n+\"\"\"Callback/closure nesting metric for tree-sitter complexity.\"\"\"\n+\n+from __future__ import annotations\n+\n+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any\n+\n+from ..imports.cache import _PARSE_CACHE\n+from .complexity_shared import ComputeFn, _ensure_parser\n+\n+if TYPE_CHECKING:\n+    from desloppify.languages._framework.treesitter import TreeSitterLangSpec\n+\n+\n+_CLOSURE_NODE_TYPES = frozenset(\n+    {\n+        \"arrow_function\",\n+        \"function_expression\",\n+        \"function\",\n+        \"lambda_expression\",\n+        \"closure_expression\",\n+        \"lambda\",\n+        \"anonymous_function\",\n+        \"block_argument\",\n+        \"func_literal\",\n+        # PHP anonymous functions (``function() { ... }``)\n+        \"anonymous_function_creation_expression\",\n+    }\n+)\n+\n+\n+def make_callback_depth_compute(spec: TreeSitterLangSpec) -> ComputeFn:\n+    \"\"\"Build a complexity compute callback for callback/closure nesting depth.\"\"\"\n+    _cached_parser: dict[str, Any] = {}\n+\n+    def compute(content: str, lines: list[str], *, _filepath: str = \"\") -> tuple[int, str] | None:\n+        del content, lines\n+        if not _filepath:\n+            return None\n+        if not _ensure_parser(_cached_parser, spec):\n+            return None\n+\n+        parser = _cached_parser[\"parser\"]\n+        cached = _PARSE_CACHE.get_or_parse(_filepath, parser, spec.grammar)\n+        if cached is None:\n+            return None\n+        _source, tree = cached\n+\n+        max_depth = 0\n+        stack: list[tuple[object, int]] = [(tree.root_node, 0)]\n+        while stack:\n+            node, depth = stack.pop()\n+            if node.type in _CLOSURE_NODE_TYPES:\n+                depth += 1\n+                if depth > max_depth:\n+                    max_depth = depth\n+            for index in range(node.child_count - 1, -1, -1):\n+                stack.append((node.children[index], depth))\n+\n+        if max_depth <= 1:\n+            return None\n+        return max_depth, f\"callback depth {max_depth}\"\n+\n+    return compute\n+\n+\n+__all__ = [\"make_callback_depth_compute\"]\n*** End Patch\n"
}

> AGENT

You’re right. This was a real bug.

Root cause:
- Review-import badge refresh could run on a **non scan-backed / subjective-only state**, and that could overwrite `scorecard.png` with a partial card (like the one showing only `Naming quality`).

What I changed:
1. Added a guard so scorecard refresh only runs when state has:
- `last_scan`, and
- at least one mechanical dimension with real checks.
2. Kept trusted-import behavior intact when scan context is valid.
3. Added tests to lock this behavior.

> DEVELOPER

did you get to the actual root of the problem?

> AGENT

Yes.

Primary root cause was a real bug in review-import plan sync: it was globally purging `subjective::*` IDs after imports with new issues, not just the imported dimensions. That happened in [`plan_sync.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/importing/plan_sync.py) and your audit log shows it firing on **2026-03-09 16:32:48 UTC** with `covered_subjective` = 20.

Secondary confusion was expected lifecycle behavior: when triage stages are present and objective backlog is empty, [`lifecycle.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/lifecycle.py) intentionally shows only workflow/triage items in `next`, which masked missing subjective queue entries.

I patched the purge bug and added a regression test in [`test_review_importing_support_direct.py`](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/review/test_review_importing_support_direct.py). The fix passed tests.

> DEVELOPER

So now will it be scan -> subjective review -> score -> triage -> keep working?

Yes, that is the intended flow now:

1. `scan`  
2. subjective review/import  
3. score workflow (`import-scores` / `communicate-score`)  
4. triage

The bug that wiped `subjective::*` queue entries after review import is fixed, so stale/below-target subjective items should stay in the plan instead of disappearing.

One caveat: `next` still applies lifecycle gating, so it may show workflow/triage first before subjective reruns depending on queue state.  
Also, because your current plan was already affected, run one fresh `desloppify scan --path .` to rehydrate `queue_order`.

You were right to flag it. I re-ran the triage flow in strict order and fixed the underlying failure.

1. Restarted triage from the beginning of triage stages: `observe -> reflect -> organize -> enrich -> sense-check`.
2. Root cause found and fixed: reflect accounting only recognized hex hash tokens in `## Coverage Ledger`, but current IDs are slug-style (and can collide), so valid reports were marked missing.
3. Patched validator + added regression tests:
- [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/validation/core.py)
- [test_triage_runner.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py)

- `pytest -q desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_runner.py` passed (`40 passed`)
- `pytest -q desloppify/tests/commands/plan/test_triage_split_modules_direct.py -k "reflect_issue_accounting or repair_reflect_report_if_needed"` passed

> AGENT

Yes, I traced it, and this is a real gap.

- `organize`/`enrich` are `self_record` stages, so the subagent runs real `plan cluster ...` mutations itself: [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L107).
- `sense-check` is different: it runs parallel content/structure prompts, merges text, then only records that merged text as the stage report: [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L113), [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L335), [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L75).
- `cmd_stage_sense_check`/`run_stage_sense_check` do validation + stage record only; they do not apply cluster edits: [stage_flow_sense_check.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_sense_check.py#L76), [stage_flow_sense_check.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_sense_check.py#L154).
- But the prompt explicitly says “The orchestrator will apply the updates.”: [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py#L66).

So the root cause is: prompt/intent says “report corrections and orchestrator applies them,” but no applier exists in the sense-check pipeline.

And yes, it should rectify. Not by letting parallel subagents mutate directly, but by having the orchestrator apply equivalent `plan cluster update`/dependency/step mutations after parsing structured sense-check output.

> DEVELOPER

So, why can't we just update it, get them to update it themselves? My understanding is that in the sense check stage, there's no overlap between the two things around. Why can't we just, one of them is
  organising, the other one is updating the data, why can't we just... make them both update the actual use the tool similar to the organize stage themselves.

> AGENT

You can, but not safely with the current implementation as-is.

1. It is currently wired as report-only.
- Sense-check prompt forbids running `desloppify` commands and says “orchestrator will apply”: [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py#L66), [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py#L73).
- Runner just merges outputs and records report text: [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L113), [orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_pipeline_execution.py#L335).
- Stage flow validates and records; no apply logic: [stage_flow_sense_check.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_sense_check.py#L76), [stage_flow_sense_check.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_sense_check.py#L154).

2. The “no overlap” assumption is the risky part.
- Content pass can change/remove steps.
- Structure pass can add cascade steps and deps across clusters: [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py#L126).
- They currently run in parallel: [orchestrator_codex_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_sense.py#L56), [orchestrator_codex_parallel.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/orchestrator_codex_parallel.py#L54).
- `--update-step N` is index-based, so concurrent edits can target stale step numbers even with per-command locks: [cluster_update.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/cluster_update.py#L51).

3. So yes, we can make it self-updating, but it needs a small redesign.
- Option A: keep report-only, add real orchestrator apply pass (deterministic).
- Option B: let subagents mutate directly, but run in 2 phases:
  1. content workers mutate only their own cluster,
  2. structure worker runs after content (serial), then stage record/confirm.

Option B is closest to what you want, and it is feasible.

High-level: the sequence now makes sense, but there is one product decision to make.

1. **Should content + structure be two separate tasks?**
- Right now they are **one queue stage** (`sense-check`) with **two internal phases** run sequentially:
  - content batches
  - then structure batch
- That is technically correct and working.
- If you want clearer operator visibility/audit, I’d split them into two explicit sub-stages (or two queue items): `sense-check-content` then `sense-check-structure`.  
  That gives cleaner “done/failed” status per phase and easier reruns.

2. **Do we check for over-engineering / confusing changes?**
- Yes, in the content prompt we explicitly ask the agent to flag net-negative work, unnecessary abstraction, and “would this make the codebase worse?” and allow removing such steps:  
  [stage_prompts_sense.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/runner/stage_prompts_sense.py:61)
- But this is still mostly **LLM judgment**, not hard policy enforcement.
- The hard validation layer checks structural quality (detail/refs/path/effort/vagueness), not semantic over-engineering:  
  [stage_flow_sense_check.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/plan/triage/stage_flow_sense_check.py:77)

So: **it’s good, but not yet “beautifully reliable” for anti-overengineering unless we add deterministic post-check rules.**  
If you want, I can implement that next (e.g., reject added steps/deps without explicit evidence + issue linkage).

> DEVELOPER

What's the root of the problem though? What would've fundamentally solved this?

> AGENT

Root cause is **state model drift**.

The system currently has multiple “truths” that can diverge:

- `plan.queue_order` (stored, mutable)
- cluster memberships (`clusters[*].issue_ids`)
- triage snapshot (`epic_triage_meta.triaged_ids`)
- skip/superseded maps
- review import outputs

Different code paths update different pieces, mostly **append/inject**, not full reconcile/prune.  
So stale IDs remain in queue, completed empty clusters linger, and ordering fragments.

What would fundamentally solve it:

1. Make queue a **derived projection**, not an authoritative mutable list.
2. Rebuild queue deterministically on every sync from canonical inputs:
   - current open issues
   - cluster assignments
   - stage state
   - skip/superseded state
   - dependency graph
3. Enforce invariants after rebuild (fail if violated):
   - no queue ID absent from canonical active issue set
   - no empty-active cluster shown as active work
   - dependency order valid
   - triage/process entries separated from work entries
4. Require structured skip reason metadata in schema.
5. Treat empty completed manual clusters as `archived` (hidden by default) rather than active scaffolding.

In one line: **single canonical model + deterministic full reconciliation** would have prevented this.

> DEVELOPER

would it have prevented this problem?

> AGENT

Yes, for the specific failure mode we just debugged, it would have prevented it.

The bug was: review import could auto-resolve old review IDs, but queue sync only ran on `new/reopened`, so stale `review::*` IDs stayed in `queue_order`.  
Now we do both:
1. Trigger review-plan sync when `auto_resolved > 0` too ([plan_sync.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/importing/plan_sync.py#L105)).  
2. Actively prune stale review IDs from queue containers during import sync ([reconcile_review_import.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/reconcile_review_import.py#L58)).

So those “2 stale queued review issues” would have been removed instead of lingering. It does not, by itself, solve separate concerns like empty speculative clusters or queue ordering quality.
